recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-40518 unless future messaging edits reintroduce mandatory response-message wording without the existing zero-or-more and no-content qualifications.
issue_request: FHIR-40518 was Published as Persuasive for FHIR-core messaging and asked to change the introduction from saying the destination returns one or more response messages to saying it returns zero or more response messages, since acknowledgments, notifications with reliable transport, and other cases might not produce a FHIR response message.
initial_application: Commit 87b1af3c094d4dd726733409d815683ceeab15c7 changed source/messaging.html from one-or-more to zero-or-more response messages for FHIR-40518, while earlier Jira-tagged commit 5e04fe1f02dae32f3f0abc945c15dade0d13a5cd only changed whitespace in the same page.
additional_context: The 2023-02-23 FHIR-I minutes record FHIR-40518 as created and found Persuasive. FHIR-27544 later treated the zero-or-more messaging-page change as the already-applied modification for a $process-message response contradiction, and AutoFHIR commit 72d53521b242d61eb956580091410fa0632d3d92 aligned the active $process-message summary and OperationDefinition description. The remaining exchange-pattern statement that request messages typically have one or more responses is qualified by nearby notification and HTTP-response exceptions, so it does not reintroduce a mandatory response-message rule.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active messaging narrative already says the destination returns zero or more response messages, and the active $process-message narrative and OperationDefinition source also use zero-or-more or no-content response semantics.
